source_audit.report:
# Automatic interleave selector under ordered N/N-1

Read-only audit, 2026-10-02. No production edits, build, engine cache or console operation. This finds an attribution mismatch in the selector's per-order score contract, not a proven explanation for the clip-reuse regression or a demonstrated performance fix. Hashes record actual inspected sources.

## Confirmed scoring contract

Generated source `game_vehicles.gen.cpp:6017+`, generator `src/game_templates.inc:20963–21033`: interleaveBegin is called during scene rendering, after earlier render work and before the deferred heavy/object phase (`game_physics.gen.cpp:1559`). It clears heavyBags/Next/Drawn, returnsfalse immediately for INTERLEAVE_PASSES=0 or splitPassActive, returns true immediately for mode2(always). Only mode1(auto) reads profTicks and RendererCore::getStallTotal. At next begin, score = unsigned wall difference minus unsigned cumulative pacing stall difference, clamped0. It calls ilAccount(score) while ilMarkActive still describes the preceding chosen order, then updates mark/stall and chooses current order.

The score is point-to-point WHOLE-loop critical-path work, not just affected passes. It includes prior scene tail, endFrame, frame-update and current scene front up to the next begin. In ordinary synchronous submission the prior frame's final GS drain is in that interval, motivating this placement; moving views/current front work can still be cross-frame noise.

ilAccount increments ilFrame. Initial ilProbing=true; probe16 frames alternating interleaved on even ilFrame, plain on odd;8 adjacent pairs. Each interleaved sample stored in ilPairOn, next plain sample records win only when ilPairOn*1.01<plainwork. Decision is ilWins*2>8, hence at least5/8 wins. Total on/off sums only log descriptive averages, not decision condition. Chosen order held100 samples before next16-frame probe. Printed integer microseconds divide ticks by295 (coarse approximation), not exact294.912; wins use raw ticks. interleaveEnd only updates heavyPrevDrawn/lastBlendAt/lastHeavy if heavyActive, not the score.

## Confirmed ordered attribution mismatch

Let B_N be interleaveBegin during EE recording frameN. Auto sample attributed to orderN is interval B_N→B_N+1 minus pacing. Under ordered execution:

1. Remaining EE records frameN after B_N.
2. RendererCore::endFrame calls Vif1Queue::endRecordingFrame; flushRecording calls completeBeforeSubmission (`vif1_queue.cpp:711–717`).
3. Callback completes/presents pending GPU jobN-1 (`renderer_core.cpp:446–468`), then permits submittingN.
4. EE update/front renderN+1 reaches B_N+1 and scores the interval as orderN.

completePipelineFrame waits DMA at449 and GS FINISH at453 BEFORE reading t0 at455. Only pacing flip/vsync t0→t1 enters stallTotal at460. Therefore any remaining DMA/GS completion of previous orderN-1 remains in the score taggedN. This is a source-established mix of current EE order and previous GPU order. At alternating probes, GPU job's order generally differs from the label of the EE recording being scored (except transitions/fallbacks). It does not establish nonzero residual GPU wait on every sample, inverted winner in this fixture, or the observed0.73–0.89ms regression mechanism. Fully hidden GPU completion would contribute zero wait; overall steady throughput score can remain useful even though per-order attribution is mixed.

Do not fix this by subtracting all DMA/GS waits: that would erase exactly a GPU-order penalty the original selector intended to price. Nor simply lag ilMarkActive byone: interval still contains EE_N and front_N+1, so one label cannot describe every component. A correct auto comparison for pipelining needs settling/block measurement or an explicit ledger tagged to the GPU job and EE work; neither is implemented by this audit.

## Other established state limitations

setFramePipeline requested flag is not activity: field/BLSS/unlimitedtriple compatibility uses synchronous path (`beginFrameRecording:425–428`). A selector cannot choose its scoring policy from getFramePipeline alone; effective pipeline mode changes matter. Overflow/foreign destructive fallback may split/drain one recording, changing which costs are hidden, without any selector mode-change notification.

No reset of ilHaveMark/ilFrame/probe sums found in generated scene load/loop. Early return for splitPassActive or mode0/2 does not update marks; later return to auto can score multiple skipped frames/views against stale order. Scene loading/reload may similarly contaminate a pair; normally100-frame hold/warm-up eventually moves beyond it, but it is not a correctly tagged sample. Source confirms stale-sample possibility, not that it contaminated the warmed clip windows. Public custom engine/settings mutations remain separate integration contracts.

The source prints decisions on choicechange or DEBUG_SHOW_PROFILER, so report frequency is not universally decision frequency. Clipfixture profiler enabled produced repeated reports; frozen observed warm regions show5 reports each, on arm2interleaved/3plain versus off5/0 and restored4/1. These are observations from separate triage, not proof that selector bias caused regression. heavy44/drawn50/blend23 remains same; reported decision rows have no explicit frame timestamp, only nearest FRAMETIME association.

## Quiet pinned controls

Use existing engine-authored meanings0plain and2always-interleaved in a private fixture; these return before clocks/probe state and avoid stale auto scoring. For sameELF runtime control, a root-only forced order gate in interleaveBegin should be resolved BEFORE auto clock/state; route false/true as mode0/2 while retaining heavy clear/setup and ordinary pixel-preserving blend safeguards. Do not change road/object order heuristics, counts, alpha/depth protections or normal submission batching. Disable auto scoring throughout those arms; never silently resume stale marks. No code proposed outside this narrow selector seam.

First establish whether plain vs interleaved matters under unchanged TyraX2: off/default code, pinnedplain / pinnedinterleaved / pinnedplain, same ELF, stationary night, warm caches after one reload perphase, independent physical boots if effectsmall. If revisiting clip candidate, compare clipoff/on/off while pinningplain in all3 phases; repeat separately with pinnedinterleaved all3 phases. Do not combine six sequential order+clip changes and label them an independent paired control without matched baselines. Archive raw work/period, same pose, frame chain/qword/copied/borrowed counts, actual chosen order and zero fallback/errors; logs should occur phase boundaries or outside raw measurement window, never perbag. No extra align3D/drain inside frame for measuring.

For block auto design after controls, use a settled run of each order rather than alternating everyframe. Exclude at least the pending-job handover plus source caching transients, collect enough samples perblock, restore reference block and compare normal critical-path work+period, with actual effective mode/scene/view changes resetting probe state. This is a plan, not a validated design: needed block length, hysteresis, moving-camera behavior and input latency must be measured, not assumed.

## Integration conclusion

This is a real compatibility gap in the old auto selector's claim that each labelled score belongs to that order under N/N-1. It is not a missing mandatory flowgraph node or an engine resource-fence failure. Preserve current experimental/default-off status; price pinned controls before changing selector. No production optimization, corrected timing or FPS benefit follows from this report.
